slides.0.title: Red wine blind-tasting practice
slides.0.subtitle: The combination of tannin and acidity often reveals the grape better than aroma
slides.1.title: Four switches for red wine deduction
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Depth of colour
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Pale: Pinot Noir, Nebbiolo, Grenache; deep: Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec. Pale colour with high tannin is Nebbiolo’s telltale paradox
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Tannin and acidity
slides.1.highlights.1.content: High tannin + high acid: Nebbiolo, Sangiovese; high tannin + medium-plus acid: Cabernet Sauvignon; low tannin + high acid: Pinot Noir, Gamay
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Varietal markers
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Blackcurrant and cedar: Cabernet; black pepper and violet: Syrah; tar and roses: Nebbiolo; sour cherry and dried herbs: Sangiovese; red cherry and forest floor: Pinot Noir
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Fruit ripeness and alcohol
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Fresh red fruit and moderate alcohol → cool or Old World; jammy, sweet black fruit and high alcohol → warm or New World; used to separate pairs such as Barossa Shiraz and northern Rhône Syrah
slides.1.content: Narrow to two or three grapes with colour and structure, then decide with aroma and ripeness.
slides.2.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Exercise 1: pale garnet with an orange rim; medium-plus nose of red cherry, dried rose, tar, liquorice and leather; dry, high acidity, high tannin, medium-plus alcohol, long finish. Deduce variety, region and approximate age.
Pale colour yet high tannin and acidity → Nebbiolo’s telltale paradox
Tar and roses → Nebbiolo’s varietal markers
Region: Barolo or Barbaresco in Piedmont
Orange rim and tertiary notes such as leather → several years or more in bottle
Quality and ageing: enough structure to keep ageing

Pale colour with high tannin and high acidity is Nebbiolo’s defining paradox, and tar and roses are its varietal markers. This structure and aroma fit Barolo or Barbaresco in Piedmont best. The orange rim and tertiary notes of leather and liquorice show several years or more in bottle. Tannin and acidity remain ample, so it can age further.

Exercise 2: deep purple-ruby; medium-plus nose of blackcurrant, blackberry, cedar, pencil shavings, vanilla and toast; dry, medium-plus acidity, high (fine) tannin, medium-plus alcohol, medium-plus body, long finish. Deduce variety and region and explain how to tell it from a Napa example.
Deep colour, blackcurrant, high tannin → Cabernet Sauvignon-led
Cedar, pencil shavings, vanilla, toast → French oak ageing
Medium-plus acidity and alcohol, fruit not overripe → moderate maritime climate
Region: Bordeaux Left Bank (e.g. Pauillac)
Versus Napa: Napa usually has riper, sweeter fruit, higher alcohol and lower acidity

Deep colour, blackcurrant and blackberry with high, fine tannins point to a Cabernet Sauvignon-led wine; cedar, pencil shavings, vanilla and toast show French oak ageing. Medium-plus acidity and alcohol with ripe but not overripe fruit fit a moderate maritime climate, most likely the Bordeaux Left Bank, such as Pauillac. Napa Cabernet usually shows riper, sweeter fruit, higher alcohol and lower acidity.

Exercise 3: deep purple-ruby; medium-plus nose of blackberry, black pepper, violet, smoked meat and olive; dry, medium-plus acidity, medium-plus tannin, medium alcohol, medium-plus body. Deduce variety and region and explain how to tell it from Barossa Shiraz.
Black pepper (rotundone) and violet → Syrah
Smoked meat and olive → cooler, Old World Syrah
Medium alcohol, medium-plus acidity → moderate climate
Region: northern Rhône (e.g. Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage)
Versus Barossa: riper, sweeter fruit, chocolate and sweet oak, higher alcohol and lower acidity

Black pepper (rotundone) and violet are Syrah’s markers; savoury smoked meat and olive with medium alcohol and medium-plus acidity point to a more moderate Old World region, best fitting the northern Rhône, such as Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage or Crozes-Hermitage. Barossa Shiraz usually shows riper, sweeter fruit with chocolate and sweet oak, higher alcohol and lower acidity.
